semin-durr:2-2.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
His saying: {الكتاب الحكيم}: it was said: faʿīl in the sense of mufʿal [passive], and this is rare; they said «أَعْقَدْتُ اللبنَ فهو عَقِيْدٌ» ("I thickened the milk, so it is thickened"), that is, «مُعْقَد». Or [faʿīl] in the sense of fāʿil [active]; or in the sense of "possessing wisdom"; or its origin is «الحكيم قائلُه» ("the one whose speaker is wise"), then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place, which is the genitive pronoun, so it turned nominative and became latent in the adjective. So said al-Zamakhsharī, and it is fine craftsmanship.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً}: the majority read it in the accusative as a ḥāl from «آيات», the governing element being the sense of the verb, or of praise, in the demonstrative. Ḥamza read it in the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. Some allowed «هدىً» to be accusative as a ḥāl while «رحمة» is nominative. He said: "Its nominative would be as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, «وهو رحمةٌ» ('and it is a mercy')." There is remoteness in this.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {الذين يُقِيمُونَ}: an adjective, or a badal, or an explicative (bayān) of what precedes it; or it is accusative or nominative by way of cutting off (qaṭʿ). On every assumption it is an explanation of iḥsān (doing good). Al-Aṣmaʿī was asked about «الألمعيّ» and recited:
3656 - الأَلْمَعِيُّ الذي يَظُنُّ بك الظْ ... ظَنَّ كأنْ قد رَأَى وقد سمعا
(The sharp-witted one is he who forms a notion about you as if he had seen and heard.)
He means that the sharp-witted one is the one who, when he supposes something, is like one who has seen and heard it.
Likewise the doers of good are those who perform these acts of obedience. Similar: some were asked about «الهَلُوع» and he did no more than recite {إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشر جَزُوعاً وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الخير مَنُوعاً} [al-Maʿārij: 20-21].

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {لَهْوَ الحديث}: it belongs to the annexation in the sense of «مِنْ» ("of"), because idle diversion (lahw) may be speech or something else, like «بابُ ساجٍ» ("a door of teak") and «جُبَّةُ خَزٍّ» ("a cloak of silk"). It was also said: it is on an omitted muḍāf, that is, "he buys the possessors of idle talk", because it was revealed concerning the buyer of singing girls. The first is more eloquent.
His saying: «لِيُضِلَّ»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «لِيَضِلَّ» with fatḥa on the prefix of the imperfect. The others read it with ḍamma, from «أضلَّ غيرَه» ("he misled another"), so its object is omitted. This necessarily entails going astray [himself], because whoever misleads has gone astray, but not conversely. That was already discussed in Sūrat Ibrāhīm. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "If you say: the reading with ḍamma is clear, because al-Naḍir's aim in buying idle talk was to turn people away from entering Islam and listening to the Qur'an and to mislead them from it; so what is the meaning of the reading with fatḥa? I say: two meanings. One: that he may persist in his error in which he was and not turn away from it, and add to it and prolong it, for the forsaken one was stubborn in his hostility to the religion and in turning people away from it. The second: that «لِيَضِلَّ» be put in the place of «لِيُضِلَّ», because whoever misleads is inevitably astray, so the follower (radīf) points to the one followed (mardūf)."
His saying: «بغير عِلْمٍ»: a ḥāl, that is, "he buys without knowledge of the conditions of trade, since he buys what causes him loss in both abodes".
His saying: «وَيَتَّخِذَها»: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read it in the accusative, conjoined to «لِيُضِلَّ», so it is a reason like the one before it. The others read it in the nominative, conjoined to «يَشْتري», so it is part of the ṣila. It was also said: the nominative is resumptive, without conjunction to the ṣila. The accusative pronoun returns to the verses mentioned earlier, or to the path (sabīl), because it takes the feminine; or to the discourses (aḥādīth) indicated by «الحديث», because it is a generic noun.
His saying: «أولئك لهم»: it was first carried on the form of «مَنْ» so it is singular, then on its meaning so it is plural, then on its form so it is singular in His saying {وَإِذَا تتلى عَلَيْهِ}. It has parallels that were pointed out in al-Māʾida at His saying the Exalted {مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ} [al-Māʾida: 60]. The Shaykh said: "We do not know of any case in the Qur'an carried on the form, then on the meaning, then on the form, other than these two verses." I say: others have been found, as I pointed out earlier in al-Māʾida.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {كَأَن لَّمْ يَسْمَعْهَا}: a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «وَلَّى» or from the pronoun in «مُسْتَكْبراً».
His saying: {كَأَنَّ في أُذُنَيْهِ وَقْراً}: a third ḥāl, or a badal for what precedes it, or a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «يَسْمَعْها», or an explication of what precedes it. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed the two comparison sentences to be resumptive.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: it is a ḥāl. The khabar of «إنَّ» is the sentence «لهم جَنَّاتُ». It is better to make «لهم» alone the khabar, with «جناتُ» its fāʿil. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «خالدون» with wāw, so it may be the khabar, and the sentence, or the prepositional phrase alone, is a ḥāl. It is also possible for «خالدون» to be a second khabar of inna.
His saying: «وَعْدَ اللَّهِ»: a maṣdar emphasizing itself, because His saying «لهم جنات» is in the sense of "Allah promised them that". And «حَقَّاً» is a maṣdar emphasizing something other than itself, that is, the content of that first sentence, and the governing element of the two differs: the implied form of the first is "Allah promised that a promise", and the implied form of the second is "It is truly so, truly".

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا}: discussed already in [Sūrat] al-Raʿd.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {مَاذَا خَلَقَ}: «ما» is interrogative. The thorough treatment of this has already been given in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:12-12.t: As for Luqmān: it was said that it is non-Arabic, and that is the apparent view; so its being diptote is due to definiteness and personal non-Arabic origin (ʿujma). It was also said: it is Arabic derived from «اللَّقْم» (swallowing), in which case it is an improvised name (murtajal), because it had no prior use among indefinite nouns. Its being diptote then is due to definiteness and the added alif and nūn.

semin-durr:13-13.t: The governing element of «إذ» is implied. «وهو يَعِظَهُ» is a circumstantial sentence. «يا بُنيَّ»: the disagreement of the reciters about it has already preceded. The discussion of {وَصَّيْنَا الإنسان} in al-ʿAnkabūt [verse 8] has also preceded.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {وَهْناً على وَهْنٍ}: it may be accusative as a ḥāl from «أمُّه», that is, "weakness upon weakness"; or from the object of «حَمَلَتْه», that is, [carrying him as] a clot, then a sperm-drop, then a morsel of flesh. Both have come in the exegesis. It was also said: accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "in weakness", said by Abū al-Baqāʾ. And «على وَهْن» is an adjective of «وَهْناً».
Al-Thaqafī, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, read {وَهَناً على وَهْنٍ} with fatḥa on the hāʾ in both. It may be that they are two dialectal forms like «الشَّعْر» and «الشَّعَر», and it may be that the fatḥa form is the maṣdar of «وَهِنَ» (with kasra), «يَوْهَنُ وَهَناً». Al-Jaḥdarī, Qatāda and Abū Rajāʾ read «وفَصْلُه» without an alif, that is, "and his weaning" (fiṭām).
His saying: «أن اشْكُرْ»: there are two views on «أنْ». The first: it is explicative (mufassira). The second: it is a maṣdar particle in the position of accusative attached to «وَصَّيْنا». That is the statement of al-Zajjāj.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {مَعْرُوفاً}: an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "companionship that is kind"; it was also said: the origin is «بمعروفٍ» ("with kindness").
His saying: «إليَّ»: attached to «أنابَ». «ثم إليَّ»: attached to an omitted element, because it is the khabar of «مَرْجِعُكم».

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ}: the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa). The conditional sentence explains the pronoun. It has been mentioned that Nāfiʿ reads «مثْقال» in the nominative, with kāna being complete (tāmma) and it being its fāʿil. On this it is asked: why was the feminine tāʾ attached to its verb? It was said: because of its annexation to a feminine, and because it is in the sense of "the weight of a grain". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that the pronoun in «إنها» refer to the small matter (hana) of evil deeds or of good deeds, in the reading of the one who made «مِثْقال» accusative. It was also said: the pronoun returns to what is understood from the context of the discourse, that is, "the thing about which you asked, if it be ...". In the exegesis: he asked his father: "Do you see a grain that falls in the depth of the sea, does Allah know it?"
ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī read «فَتَكِنَّ» with kasra on the kāf and a fatḥa-vowelled doubled nūn, that is, "so it settles". Muḥammad ibn Abī Fajja al-Baʿlabakkī read «فَتُكَنَّ» likewise except that it is passive. Qatāda read «فَتَكِنُ» with kasra on the kāf and a lightened nūn, the imperfect of «وَكَنَ», that is, it settled in its nest («وَكْنِه» and «وَكْرِه»).

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {مِنْ عَزْمِ}: «عَزْم» is a maṣdar. It may be in the sense of mafʿūl, that is, "of the matters resolved upon", or in the sense of ʿāzim as in His saying {فَإِذَا عَزَمَ الأمر} [Muḥammad: 21], and that is an eloquent figure. Al-Mubarrad claimed that the ʿayn is substituted by ḥāʾ, saying «حَزْمٌ» and «عَزْمٌ». The sound view is that they are two different roots that agree in meaning.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تُصَعِّرْ}: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and the two brothers read «تُصاعِرْ» with an alif and lightened ʿayn. The others read it without alif and with doubled ʿayn; the orthography admits both, since the orthography is without alif. They are two dialects: the Hijazi dialect is the lightened form, and Tamīm use the doubled form. From the doubled form is his saying:
3657 - وكُنَّا إذا الجبارُ صَعَّر خَدَّه ... أقَمْنا له مِنْ مَيْلِه فَيُقَوَّمُ
(When the tyrant turned his cheek away in disdain, we straightened his inclination for him and he was set straight.)
It is also said «تَصَعَّر». He said:
3658 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... أَقَمْنا له مِنْ خَدِّه المُتَصَعِّرِ
(... we straightened for him his cheek that was turned in disdain.)
It is from inclining (mayl), because the arrogant one tilts his cheek in pride, as in His saying {ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ} [al-Ḥajj: 9]. Abū ʿUbayda said: "Its origin is from «الصَّعَر», a disease that strikes camels in their necks so they tilt and twist." Al-Yazīdī's explanation of it as speaking with exaggerated mouth movements (al-tashaddūq fī al-kalām) does not agree with the verse here.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {واقصد}: this is intransitive, in the sense of «اقتصِدْ» ("be moderate") and "follow the middle way between that, a just course". It was also read «وأَقْصِدْ» with a hamzat al-qaṭʿ, from «أَقْصَدَ» when one aims his arrow at the target.
His saying: «مِنْ صَوْتِك»: partitive. According to al-Akhfash it may be redundant, and {يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَاتَهُمْ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 3] supports it. It was also said: «من صوتك» is an adjective of an omitted described noun, that is, "something of your voice". The Jāhiliyya used to boast of raising the voice. He said:
3659 - جَهيرُ الكلامِ جَهيرُ العُطاس ... جَهيرُ الرُّواءِ جَهيرُ النِّعَمْ
(Loud of speech, loud of sneeze, loud of appearance, loud of blessings.)
His saying: «إنَّ أَنْكَرَ»: it was said that «أنكَر» is passive in form, like «أَشْغَلُ مِنْ ذاتِ النَّحْيَيْن» ("busier than the woman with the two skins"). There is disagreement about it. «صوت» is singular because the genus is intended and because it is annexed to a plural.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {نِعَمَهُ}: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and Ḥafṣ read «نِعَمَه», the plural of «نِعْمة» annexed to the pronoun hāʾ, so «ظاهرةً» is a ḥāl from it. The others read «نِعْمةً» with sukūn on the ʿayn and tanwīn on the feminine tāʾ, a generic noun by which the plural is meant, so «ظاهرة» is an adjective of it. Ibn ʿAbbās and Yaḥyā ibn ʿUmāra read «وأَصْبَغَ» with the sīn replaced by ṣād. This is the dialect of Kalb; they do that with ghayn, khāʾ and qāf. The like of all these sentences has preceded in al-Baqara, and the discussion of «أَوَلَوْ» and the like.

semin-durr:22-22.t: ʿAlī and al-Sulamī read it «يُسَلِّم» with doubling.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {والبحر}: Abū ʿAmr read it in the accusative; the others in the nominative. The accusative has two analyses. The first: conjunction to the ism of «أنَّ», that is, "and if the sea", with «يَمُدُّه» as the khabar. The second: accusative by an implied verb which «يمدُّه» explains, and the wāw is then the wāw of ḥāl. The sentence is circumstantial, and no linking pronoun between the ḥāl and its owner was needed, since the wāw makes it unnecessary. The implied form: "even if what is on the earth [were pens], the sea being supplied with such-and-such".
As for the nominative, it has two analyses. The first: conjunction to «أنَّ» and what lies within its scope. You have already seen concerning the «أنَّ» that occurs after «لو» two positions: the position of Sībawayh, nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the position of al-Mubarrad, nominative as a fāʿil of an implied verb; both apply here. According to Sībawayh's position, the implied conjunction is: "and if the sea". Except that the Shaykh said: a mubtadaʾ that is an explicit noun does not follow «لو» except in necessity (ḍarūra), as in his saying:
3660 - لو بغير الماءِ حَلْقي شَرِقٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Were my throat choking on something other than water ...)
and this statement leads to that. Then he answered that what is not tolerated in the element conjoined to is tolerated in the conjoined element, as in their saying «رُبَّ رجلٍ وأخيه يقولان ذلك» ("many a man and his brother say that"). According to al-Mubarrad's position the implied form is: "and if the sea were established", and on both assumptions «يمدُّه» is a circumstantial sentence from «البحر».
The second: «البحر» is a mubtadaʾ and «يَمُدُّه» the khabar, the sentence being circumstantial as has preceded in the sentence of ishtighāl, the link being the wāw. Al-Zamakhsharī made it a question and answer. And he recited: 3661 - وقد أَغْتَدِيْ والطيرُ في وُكُناتِها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I may set out in the morning while the birds are still in their nests ...)
And «مِنْ شجَرة» is a ḥāl: either from the relative noun, or from the latent pronoun in the prepositional phrase that serves as ṣila; and «أقلامٌ» is the khabar of «أنَّ». The Shaykh said: "In it is evidence against those who say, like al-Zamakhsharī and those of the non-Arabs who side with him, that the khabar of «أنَّ» occurring after «لو» is never a noun, neither inert nor derived, but must be a verb." He said: "That is false", and recited:
3662 - ولو أنها عُصْفورَةٌ لَحَسِبْتُها ... مُسَوَّمَةً تَدْعو عبيداً وأَزْنَما
(Even if it were a sparrow, I would reckon it a marked [horse] calling ʿUbayd and Azmam.)
And he said:
3663 - ما أطيبَ العَيْشَ لو أنَّ الفتى حَجَرٌ ... تَنْبُو الحوادِثُ عنه وهْو مَلْمُومُ
(How pleasant life would be if a man were a stone from which misfortunes glance off, compact.)
And he said:
3664 - ولو أنَّ حياً فائتُ الموتِ فاته ... أخو الحربِ فوقَ القارِحِ العَدَوانِ
(Even if a living being could escape death, the warrior on a swift full-grown horse would have escaped it.)
He said: "It is frequent in their speech." I say: it was mentioned at the beginning of this subject that this verse and the like invalidate the apparent statement of the earlier scholars about «لو», that it is a particle of "impossibility due to impossibility", since a grave difficulty follows: what comes after it, when it is negative in form, is affirmative in meaning, and conversely. And His saying «ما نَفِدَتْ» is negative in form; were it affirmative in meaning, the meaning would be corrupted. So you should consult the beginning of al-Baqara.
ʿAbd Allāh [Ibn Masʿūd] read «وبَحْرٌ» indefinite, and it has the same two analyses as the definite. What justified beginning with an indefinite is its occurrence after the wāw of ḥāl, which is counted among the justifications for beginning with an indefinite. They recited:
3665 - سَرَيْنا ونجمٌ قد أضاء فَمُذْ بَدا ... مُحَيَّاك أخفى ضَوْءُه كلَّ شارِقِ
(We travelled by night while a star shone; then when your face appeared, its light hid every rising [star].)
By this the invalidity is evident of the statement of one who said that in this reading the claim of conjunction to «أنَّ» is necessary, as though he imagined that there is no justification there.
ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy read «تَمُدُّه» in the feminine because of «سبعة». Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Hurmuz and Ibn Muṣarrif read «يُمِدُّه» with a ḍamma-vowelled yāʾ from below and kasra on the mīm, from «أمَدَّه». The two dialectal forms were already discussed at the end of al-Aʿrāf and the beginning of al-Baqara.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it said «مِنْ شجرة» in the singular? I say: the detailing of the trees was intended, going through them tree by tree, so that no single tree of the genus remains but has been cut into pens." The Shaykh said: "It is a case of the singular standing in the place of the plural and the indefinite in the place of the definite, as in {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 106]." I say: this removes the meaning that al-Zamakhsharī showed. He also said: "If you say: «الكلمات» is a plural of paucity while the place calls for plural of multitude, why was «كَلِم» not said? I say: its meaning is that the seas do not suffice to write His 'words' (kalimāt), so how [could they suffice for] His 'word-multitudes' (kalim)?" I say: he means that it is of the category of a fortiori inference. The Shaykh rejected it: whenever the sound plural is made definite by «أل» not of the covenant kind, or is annexed, it is general. I say: people disagree about «أل» as to whether it gives generality or not. Al-Zamakhsharī may be among those who do not hold generality. People have continued to ask about the verse of Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him: 3666 - لنا الجَفَناتُ الغُرُّ يَلْمَعْنَ بالضُّحى ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(We have the bright bowls that gleam at forenoon ...)
and they say: how did he use the plural of paucity in a context of praise, and why did he not say «الجِفان»? This confirms what al-Zamakhsharī said and concedes that «أل» does not produce multitude in the plural of paucity.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ كَنَفْسٍ}: the khabar of «ما خَلْقُكم», and the implied form: "except like the creation of one single soul and its resurrection". Here it is «إلى أَجَل» and in al-Zumar {لأَجَلٍ} [verse 5], because both meanings suit the two particles, so it does not matter to you in which it occurs.

semin-durr:29-29.t: Abū ʿAmr read in one transmission {وَأَنَّ الله بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ} with the yāʾ of the third person. The others read it with the tāʾ of the second person as an address.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {بِنِعْمَةِ الله}: it may be attached to «تَجْري» or to an omitted element as a ḥāl, that is, "accompanied by the favour of Allah". Al-Aʿmash and al-Aʿraj read «بنِعْمات» in the plural. Ibn Abī ʿAbla likewise, except that he put fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the ʿayn. Mūsā ibn al-Zubayr read «الفُلُك» with two ḍammas.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {خَتَّارٍ}: an intensive pattern from «الخَتْر», which is the most severe treachery. Al-Aʿshā said: 3667 - بأبلقِ الفَرْدِ مِنْ تَيْماءَ مَنْزِلُه ... حِصْنٌ حَصينٌ وجارٌ غيرُ خَتَّار
(In Ablaq al-Fard of Taymāʾ is his dwelling, a stout fortress, and a neighbour not treacherous.)
And ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib said:
3668 - فإنَّك لو رَأَيْتَ أبا عُمَيْرٍ ... مَلأْتَ يَدَيْكَ مِنْ غَدْرٍ وخَتْرِ
(For if you saw Abū ʿUmayr, you would fill your hands with perfidy and treachery.)
They said: "If you extend to us a span of perfidy, we will extend to you a cubit of treachery.""

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ مَوْلُودٌ}: they allowed two views on it. The first: it is a mubtadaʾ and what follows is the khabar. The second: it is conjoined to «والدٌ», and the sentence is an adjective of it. There is a difficulty in it: He negated that he [the father] would compensate, then described him as compensating. It may be answered that although he may compensate on his behalf in this world, he does not compensate on his behalf on the Day of Resurrection, so the two states are with respect to two times.
Al-Mahdawī forbade it to be a mubtadaʾ, saying: "because the sentence after it is an adjective of it, so it would remain without a khabar, and there is no justification other than the adjective." That is an oversight, because an indefinite noun, whenever it depends on a negation, may be the beginning of a sentence; and this is among the best-known justifications for it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: His saying {وَلاَ مَوْلُودٌ هُوَ جَازٍ عَن وَالِدِهِ شَيْئاً} comes in a manner of emphasis that did not apply to what is conjoined to it. I say: so it is, because the nominal sentence is stronger than the verbal, and there is added to that His saying «هو» and His saying «مولود»." He said: "The sense of emphasis in the word «المولود» is that were one of them to intercede for the nearest father from whom he was born, it would not be accepted from him, let alone that he intercede for those above him among his grandfathers, because «الولد» applies to the child and the child's child, unlike «المولود», which is for the one born from you." He said: "The reason it came in this manner is that the address is to the believers, whose fathers died in disbelief, so the aim was to cut off their hopes and the hopes of people concerning them."
The sentence «لا يَجْزِي» is an adjective of «يومٍ», and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, «فيه» ("in it"); it was omitted entirely, or by degrees.
ʿIkrima read «لا يُجْزَى» passive. Abū al-Sammāl and Abū al-Siwār read «لا يُجْزِئ» with hamza, from «أَجْزأ عنه», that is, "sufficed for him".
His saying: «شيئاً»: accusative as a maṣdar, and it is a case of iʿmāl (assigning the governing role), because «يَجْزي» and «جازٍ» both require it; the governing element is «جازٍ», according to the preferred view of omission from the first.
His saying: «فلا تَغُرَّنَّكُمْ»: the majority read it with doubled nūn. Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Yaʿqūb read it with the light nūn. Simāk ibn Ḥarb and Yaʿqūb read «الغُرور» with ḍamma, which is a maṣdar, while the majority read it with fatḥa, a pattern of intensive adjective like «شَكُور». It was explained as the devil, though it is possible that the ḍamma form is a maṣdar serving as a description of the devil.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {مَّاذَا تَكْسِبُ}: «ما» may be interrogative, in which case it suspends «الدِّراية» ("knowing"); or relative, in which case it is accusative by it. The ruling on «ماذا» is already known from the beginning of the book and has been repeated throughout.
His saying: «بأيِّ أرضٍ»: attached to «تموتُ», and it suspends «الدِّراية», so it is in the position of accusative. Mūsā al-Aswārī read «بأيةِ أرضٍ» with its feminine. That is a weak dialect, like the feminine of «كل», where they said «كلتهن», and he suspended that. The bāʾ is locative, in the sense of «في», that is, "in a land", like «زيد بمكة» ("Zayd is in Mecca"), that is, in it.
